nama_domain: 'AI+' National Policy & Mass AI Diffusion — the state-orchestrated, target-driven diffusion of AI into every sector of the economy and society (as distinct from AI research/model-building policy), measured by binding penetration targets, sectoral action plans, compute subsidies, and population-scale consumer adoption
kategori: Regulasi & Kebijakan (Regulation & Policy) — specifically industrial/diffusion policy and digital-governance architecture, with heavy spillovers into Digital Economy, Public Administration, Education Policy, and Labor Policy
tahun_mulai_china: Layered origin. (1) INSTITUTIONAL ROOTS: 'Internet+' (互联网+) written into the Government Work Report in March 2015 — the direct template for 'AI+' as a policy genre; the New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan (国务院, July 2017) set the 2030 'world leader in AI' goal. (2) THE 'AI+' TERM ITSELF: first appeared in the Government Work Report in March 2024. (3) THE DECISIVE MOMENT — the subject of this research: 26-27 August 2025, when the State Council issued the 'Opinions on Deepening the Implementation of the Artificial Intelligence+ Initiative' (关于深入实施'人工智能+'行动的意见), the first document anywhere to attach HARD NUMERIC PENETRATION TARGETS to economy-wide AI adoption. (4) OPERATIONALISATION: 2026 — the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030, adopted March 2026) absorbed AI+ as a core pillar; MOE's 'AI+ Education' action plan (10 April 2026); MOFCOM's 'AI+ Consumption' implementation opinions (18 June 2026); MIIT's 'AI+ Manufacturing' special action (announced Nov 2025, running through 2027). The demand-side precondition landed in January-February 2025 when DeepSeek-R1 collapsed domestic inference costs, making a 70%-penetration target arithmetically conceivable rather than aspirational.
pemain_kunci_china:
STATE / POLICY ACTORS: State Council (issuer of the 'AI+' Opinions, 26-27 Aug 2025, and owner of the 70%/90%/2035 targets); National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC — lead coordinator, 'AI+' scenario lists); Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT — 'AI+ Manufacturing' special action with eight other agencies; >50 national and industry AI standards targeted by 2026); Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM — 'AI+ Consumption' opinions, 18 June 2026, with seven other departments); Ministry of Education (MOE — 'AI+ Education' action plan, 10 April 2026, full system build-out by 2030); Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC — the governance counterweight: generative-AI interim measures 2023, AI content-labelling measures effective 1 Sept 2025, AI anthropomorphic-interaction/companion measures issued 10 April 2026 effective 15 July 2026); National Data Bureau (Liu Liehong — publishes national token-consumption metrics as a diffusion KPI); SASAC and central SOEs (mandated early adopters); provincial and municipal governments (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Guangdong — compute vouchers 算力券, model vouchers 模型券, corpus subsidies).

MODEL / PLATFORM COMPANIES: ByteDance (Doubao — the single largest diffusion vehicle, 157m MAU Aug 2025 rising to 382m by May 2026, and >1.2 trillion tokens/day by April 2026); DeepSeek (open-weight R1/V3 — the cost collapse that made mass diffusion economically possible; 143m MAU Aug 2025); Alibaba (Qwen/Tongyi — 167m MAU May 2026, largest open-weight derivative ecosystem globally; Alibaba Cloud as the export arm into Southeast Asia); Tencent (Yuanbao, Hunyuan, enterprise AI); Moonshot (Kimi), Zhipu AI, MiniMax, StepFun, Baidu (Ernie), iFlytek (education/healthcare verticals), Huawei (Ascend compute + Pangu industrial models — the state-preferred full-stack vendor).

DIFFUSION INFRASTRUCTURE: national integrated computing network ('East Data West Computing'); intelligent computing centres (1.59 million PFLOPS installed by end-2025); QuestMobile and CNNIC (the measurement apparatus that makes penetration legible and therefore governable); the 1 trillion RMB state venture capital fund for AI, robotics and frontier tech under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
apa_yang_terjadi_di_china:
China has converted AI from an innovation policy into a DIFFUSION policy — and in doing so has become the first country to set quantified, government-owned adoption targets for a general-purpose technology across the whole economy. Five mechanisms make it work.

(1) A TARGET ARCHITECTURE, NOT A VISION STATEMENT. The State Council's 'AI+' Opinions (26-27 Aug 2025) is deliberately modelled on 'Internet+' (2015), but where 'Internet+' was directional, 'AI+' is numeric: penetration of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents to exceed 70% by 2027 and 90% by 2030, with AI becoming a principal driver of growth by 2030 and a 'fully intelligent economy and society' by 2035. Six domains are named — science and technology, industrial development, consumption, people's wellbeing/public welfare, governance, and global cooperation. Because the targets are numeric and dated, they can be cascaded to ministries, provinces and SOEs as performance indicators, which is the entire point: in the Chinese system, what is measured and assigned is what gets built.

(2) CASCADE INTO SECTORAL ACTION PLANS. The umbrella document is deliberately thin; the operative content arrives in ministry-level implementation plans issued through 2026. MIIT and eight agencies run the 'AI+ Manufacturing' special action to 2027 with concrete deliverables — 3 to 5 general-purpose industrial foundation models, 1,000 industrial intelligent agents, 100 high-quality manufacturing datasets, 500 demonstration scenarios. MOFCOM and seven departments issued 'AI+ Consumption' implementation opinions (18 June 2026) covering retail, tourism, hospitality and services. MOE issued an 'AI+ Education' action plan (10 April 2026) building an AI education system from primary school to university with full implementation by 2030. NDRC maintains lists of 'strategic high-value scenarios' (reported at around 40) that direct where deployment effort goes. MIIT targets more than 50 national and industry AI standards by 2026 — standards being the quiet instrument that makes enterprise procurement safe and therefore fast.

(3) SUBSIDISED DEMAND, NOT JUST SUBSIDISED SUPPLY. This is the most copyable innovation. Provinces issue compute vouchers (算力券), model vouchers (模型券) and corpus/data subsidies that pay firms to CONSUME AI rather than only paying labs to build it. Shanghai alone committed roughly 900 million CNY for access to computing clusters, models and training data plus around 500 million CNY over three to five years for enterprise innovation. Because the binding constraint on diffusion is buyer-side cost and risk, not seller-side capability, demand subsidies move penetration faster than R&D grants.

(4) A CONSUMER FLYWHEEL RUNNING AHEAD OF THE POLICY. Mass adoption was not created by the plan — it was already happening and the plan rides it. CNNIC's 57th report (5 Feb 2026) puts generative-AI users at 602 million, 42.8% of the population, up 141.7% year-on-year from 249 million (17.6%) at end-2024. China's AI-native apps reached 499 million MAU by May 2026, +85.4% YoY, with users averaging 92.7 sessions and 183 minutes per month. Daily national token consumption rose from about 100 billion in early 2024 to 1.4 trillion by March 2026 — more than a thousandfold in two years — a metric the National Data Bureau now publishes precisely because it is the cleanest available proxy for diffusion. Free-to-user pricing (Doubao, DeepSeek, Qwen all free at the consumer tier) is itself an implicit subsidy that no other market has matched at this scale.

(5) GOVERNANCE APPLIED TO HARMS, NOT TO ADOPTION. Uniquely, China is simultaneously the world's most aggressive AI-adoption promoter AND one of its most prescriptive AI regulators — but the regulation targets specific harms rather than the diffusion itself. AI-generated content labelling became mandatory on 1 September 2025. The Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services (issued 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR; effective 15 July 2026) banned virtual-companion and virtual-family services for minors, required guardian consent for users under 14, and imposed anti-addiction and safety-assessment duties — forcing ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen to shut down personalised companion agents used by very large user bases. Notably, the same interim measures explicitly EXEMPT customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education and research — i.e. the regulator carved out exactly the productivity uses the AI+ plan is trying to scale. The AI+ Opinions themselves instruct officials to 'strengthen employment risk assessments for AI applications' and to steer innovation resources toward job-creating directions, and an 'AI + Employment' framework (tax incentives, reskilling, wage subsidies) is under discussion.

The net effect is a state that treats AI penetration as infrastructure policy — comparable to electrification or highway build-out — with quantified coverage targets, subsidised uptake, standardised interfaces, sectoral rollout plans, and a separate harm-specific regulatory track that does not slow the rollout.
data_skala_china:
POLICY TARGETS. State Council 'AI+' Opinions (26-27 Aug 2025): penetration of new-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents >70% by 2027, >90% by 2030; AI a principal engine of economic growth by 2030; 'fully intelligent economy and society' by 2035. Six named domains. MIIT: >50 national/industry AI standards by 2026. 'AI+ Manufacturing' (to 2027): 3-5 general-purpose industrial models, 1,000 industrial intelligent agents, 100 high-quality manufacturing datasets, 500 demonstration scenarios. MOE 'AI+ Education' (10 Apr 2026): full system implementation by 2030. NDRC: ~40 'strategic high-value scenarios' [uncertain — scenario-list count varies by reporting].

INDUSTRY SCALE. Core AI industry >1.2 trillion yuan in 2025 (~US$174bn), +40% YoY; 2026 growth projected above 30%. AI companies: >6,200 (2025), >6,600 by June 2026, roughly 15% of the global total. State VC fund of 1 trillion RMB for AI/robotics/frontier tech under the 15th Five-Year Plan; RMB 100 billion special fund in the 2026 Government Work Report to stimulate domestic demand [uncertain — this fund is broader than AI].

COMPUTE & USAGE. Intelligent computing power 1.59 million PFLOPS by end-2025, second globally; intelligent computing projected above 35% of total computing capacity in 2026. Daily national token invocation 1.4 trillion (March 2026, National Data Bureau) versus ~100 billion in early 2024 — a >1,000x increase in two years; ByteDance's Doubao alone exceeded 1.2 trillion tokens/day by April 2026. On OpenRouter, Chinese open models contributed ~1.296 trillion tokens globally in the first week of April 2026, ahead of US models for five consecutive weeks [uncertain — OpenRouter is a partial, non-representative sample of global inference].

CONSUMER PENETRATION (CNNIC 57th report, 5 Feb 2026). Netizens 1.125 billion. Generative-AI users 602 million, 42.8% penetration, +141.7% YoY; up from 249 million (17.6%) at end-2024 and 515 million at mid/late-2025. Analysts project >900 million by end-2026 [uncertain — third-party projection].

APP-LEVEL (QuestMobile). August 2025: Doubao 157 million MAU (+6.6% MoM), DeepSeek 143 million (-4% MoM); roughly 40% of users leaving DeepSeek in May 2025 migrated to Doubao. March 2026: AI-native apps 440 million MAU total; Doubao 345m, Qwen 166m, DeepSeek 127m. May 2026: AI-native apps 499 million MAU (+85.4% YoY); Doubao 382m, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m; average 92.7 uses and 183 minutes per user per month; Doubao 54.8 sessions/month (+22 YoY).

ENTERPRISE DIFFUSION. By end-2025, >30% of above-scale manufacturing enterprises (annual main-business revenue ≥20 million yuan) had adopted AI technologies. Enterprise AI-agent deployment reported at roughly 79% of surveyed enterprises with ~23% at full production scale, penetration >30% in finance and e-commerce and ~20% in manufacturing [uncertain — survey-based, definitions vary]. A counterweight datapoint: in 2022 only 4.5% of surveyed SOE executives said internal digital transformation was 'meeting expectations' and 60% said their firms were at an early stage — the SOEs the state most wants to lead adoption are the least digitised.

REGULATORY MILESTONES. AI content-labelling measures effective 1 Sept 2025. AI Anthropomorphic Interaction (companion) Interim Measures: issued 10 April 2026 by five agencies, effective 15 July 2026; minors barred from virtual companion/family services; guardian consent required under 14; Doubao and Qwen shut personalised companion agents. Youth (16-24, ex-students) unemployment 18.9% (Aug 2025) easing to 16.9% (March 2026) — the political constraint the diffusion policy must manage.
fase_tren_di_china: BOOMING and STATE-ACCELERATED, entering the mid-phase of a policy cycle that is unusual for running adoption and harm-regulation on parallel tracks. Sequence: policy formation (Mar 2024 'AI+' named in the Government Work Report) → mandate issued (Aug 2025 State Council Opinions with numeric targets) → operationalisation and cascade (2026: 15th Five-Year Plan absorption, MOE/MOFCOM/MIIT sectoral plans, provincial voucher schemes, standards build-out) → the 2027 checkpoint (70% target) → saturation target 2030 (90%) → declared endpoint 2035. Consumer adoption is in explosive growth (42.8% population penetration, +141.7% YoY) and shows no plateau. Simultaneously the harm-regulation track is already in ENFORCEMENT phase — content labelling live since Sept 2025 and companion-AI restrictions live since July 2026 with real product shutdowns — which is remarkable: China is regulating specific AI harms while its penetration curve is still steepening, rather than after saturation as it did with platforms (2020-2022) and fintech. There is no backlash phase against diffusion itself; the visible backlash is narrow and targeted (minors, emotional dependence, deepfakes, employment displacement).
puncak_tren_china: The POLICY peak is dated by the plan itself: 2027 is the first hard checkpoint (70%) and 2030 the saturation target (90%), with 2035 as the declared 'intelligent society' endpoint. The 2026-2027 window is where the mandate bites hardest, because that is when provinces, ministries and SOEs must show progress against the 2027 number — expect the most intense procurement, subsidy and demonstration-project activity in that period. The CONSUMER adoption curve most likely inflects (moves from explosive to incremental growth) around 2027-2028 as generative-AI penetration approaches 60-70% of the population and saturates against the 1.125 billion netizen ceiling. Geographic epicentres: Beijing (policy, models, Zhongguancun), Hangzhou (Alibaba, DeepSeek, the 'Six Little Dragons'), Shanghai (largest subsidy programme, WAIC, finance and services deployment), Shenzhen (hardware, terminals, robotics), Guangdong-Jiangsu-Zhejiang (AI+ Manufacturing). Sectoral peaks will be earliest in consumer internet, finance, e-commerce and government services, and latest in heavy-industry SOEs where digitisation is weakest. [uncertain — peak timing is a projection anchored on stated targets, and official penetration claims for 2027 will be difficult to verify independently]
status_di_indonesia: BELUM ADA PADANAN KEBIJAKAN (NO EQUIVALENT POLICY YET) — the sharpest institutional gap in this entire research series. Indonesia has strategy documents but no diffusion mandate: no numeric penetration target, no sectoral action plans, no compute or model vouchers, no dedicated budget line, and — as of August 2026 — not even a signed Presidential Regulation. The two draft Perpres (National AI Roadmap and AI Ethics/Governance) have slipped at least three announced deadlines (early 2026 → H1 2026 → still awaiting the President's signature). On the CONSUMER side, however, Indonesia is not absent: roughly 42-43 million Indonesians have used generative AI, and Indonesia is a top-15 ChatGPT market globally. The pattern is therefore MARKET-LED DIFFUSION WITHOUT STATE ORCHESTRATION — the mirror image of China.
contoh_konkret_indonesia:
STRATEGY DOCUMENTS (non-binding). Strategi Nasional Kecerdasan Artifisial (Stranas KA) 2020-2045, launched August 2020 — four focus areas (ethics/policy, talent, infrastructure/data, industrial research) and five priority sectors (health, bureaucratic reform, education and research, food security, mobility/smart cities), but no enforceable standards, no dedicated implementing agency, and no monitoring mechanism. Komdigi Circular Letter (Surat Edaran) No. 9/2023 on AI ethics — voluntary, unenforceable.

THE PENDING PERPRES. Komdigi's National AI Roadmap White Paper (179 pages, public consultation from August 2025) and two draft Presidential Regulations: (a) National AI Roadmap (variously reported as 2026-2029 and 2026-2030) and (b) AI Ethics/Governance with a three-tier risk classification and harm-mitigation duties. Contents reported from the drafts: government bodies to adopt AI progressively across 2026-2029; AI projected to add up to 12% to GDP (~US$366 billion) by 2030; mandatory reporting of AI-related risks including biometric misuse, IP violation and deepfakes; AI-generated content labelling/watermarking as the FIRST implementing regulation; a 'Sovereign AI Fund' to be established 2027-2029 and managed primarily by Danantara (the sovereign wealth manager overseeing >US$900bn in state assets) using blended public-private finance for fundamental research, public-sector pilots, and data/compute infrastructure. As of August 2026 neither Perpres has been signed; Komdigi has said both cleared harmonisation and sit at the State Secretariat.

EIGHT 'QUICK WIN' PROJECTS (from the white paper): AI monitoring of the Makan Bergizi Gratis free nutritious-meal programme (~US$15bn, 83 million beneficiaries — attendance tracking and meal distribution), crop-yield forecasting for food self-sufficiency, and financial-report tracking inside the Koperasi Desa Merah Putih programme, among others.

GOVTECH. INA Digital / GovTech national rollout scheduled for October 2026 under President Prabowo, AI-supported, with roughly 80% of the system already connected and AI-processed data integration implemented across eight ministries and agencies.

SOVEREIGN CAPABILITY. Sahabat-AI — Indonesia's open-source LLM built by Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison with GoTo and Nvidia support, covering Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages, released as a consumer app on Android and iOS in February 2026 and endorsed by Komdigi as aligned with the national roadmap. AI Center of Excellence with Indosat, Nvidia and Cisco (target: 1 million Indonesians with digital/AI skills by 2027). Komdigi's AI Talent Factory under the Digital Talent Development Centre. BDx Indonesia's sovereign AI data centre (Dec 2024) and Indosat's AI Factory — the first in Southeast Asia to integrate Nvidia GB200 NVL72 systems.

EDUCATION. Permendikdasmen No. 13/2025 made Coding and Artificial Intelligence an OPTIONAL subject from the 2025/2026 school year, phased in at grade 5 (SD), grade 7 (SMP) and grade 10 (SMA/SMK); explicitly not compulsory for schools lacking facilities. Teacher self-paced coding/AI training participation reported at 97% by July 2026; ImajiNation 2026 competition targeting 11,000+ participants from 2,000 schools across 38 provinces.

CHINA VECTOR. Indonesia became a FOUNDING MEMBER of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO) in Shanghai on 17 July 2026, alongside 28 other economies, signed by Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto — the single clearest signal of policy alignment with the Chinese AI-governance bloc. Chinese counterparts engaged: ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent, Huawei, Deep Robotics, Unitree, FiberHome. Tencent has introduced enterprise AI products to J&T Express, Traveloka and GDP Venture; a Joint Laboratory for Digital Medicine and Proactive Health has been established; a Tsinghua University AI-focused branch campus has been proposed; AIonOS and Indosat are building DeepSeek-powered solutions for tourism, knowledge economy and sustainable agriculture.
data_skala_indonesia:
CONSUMER ADOPTION. APJII 2026 survey: internet penetration 81.72% — 235,261,078 users of a 287,303,234 population (up from 80.66%). Of those internet users, only 18.2% have ever used AI; 81.8% never have. That implies roughly 42-43 million generative-AI users, about 14.9% of the total population. Gen Z is the most active cohort. Indonesia nonetheless ranks in the global top 15 for ChatGPT users and is described as Southeast Asia's fastest-growing ChatGPT market (~85% growth) [uncertain — vendor/third-party estimate].

DIRECT COMPARISON WITH CHINA. Indonesia ~14.9% population penetration of generative AI (2026) versus China 42.8% (Dec 2025) and 17.6% (Dec 2024). Indonesia's internet penetration (81.72%) is HIGHER than China's (~80%), so the gap is not connectivity — it is usage, language fit, digital literacy, and the absence of a free, locally-tuned, mass-market assistant of the Doubao type.

ENTERPRISE. Organizational AI implementation ~26% (Pertama Partners SEA Mid-Market AI Adoption Index 2026); ~23% of enterprises at the AI 'investment' stage (IBM/Advisia); versus China's >30% of above-scale manufacturers and ~79% enterprise agent deployment. Some vendor material claims '62% of Indonesian companies will adopt AI' and even '92% workplace AI adoption — the world's highest' [both almost certainly vendor-marketing figures measuring intent or any-use rather than implementation; not credible as adoption statistics].

STATE CAPACITY AND MONEY. No published national AI diffusion budget. The Sovereign AI Fund is proposed for 2027-2029 with no committed figure; Danantara manages >US$900bn in state assets. Compare China: 1 trillion RMB state VC fund, Shanghai alone committing ~1.4 billion CNY in municipal AI subsidies. Indonesia attracted roughly US$4.6 billion in AI-related investment 2020-2024 (first in Southeast Asia) and US$542.9 million specifically into AI startups by 2024 (+141.5% over five years).

COMPUTE. ~580 MW of operating data-centre capacity with ~1.3 GW of additional capacity sought; Indonesia's first sovereign AI data centre (BDx, Dec 2024); Indosat AI Factory with Nvidia GB200 NVL72; Nvidia's US$200 million AI centre. China: 1.59 million PFLOPS of intelligent compute installed by end-2025.

TALENT. Requirement of 9 million digital talents by 2030 (World Bank/McKinsey basis) against university output of roughly 100,000-200,000 per year — a shortfall of 400,000-500,000 annually. AI Center of Excellence target: 1 million Indonesians with digital skills by 2027.

RANKING. Indonesia placed 49th in the 2024 Global AI Index of 122 indicators — behind Singapore (3rd), Malaysia (39th) and Thailand (43rd), ahead of Vietnam (58th).

ECONOMIC PROJECTIONS (from the draft roadmap and market research, all contested): AI could add 12% to GDP / US$366 billion by 2030; AI adoption could raise GDP contribution by 3.67%; the Indonesian AI market projected at ~US$10.9 billion by 2030; digital economy heading toward ~US$180 billion by 2030 [uncertain — these are projections from different methodologies and are not mutually consistent].
estimasi_lag_tahun:
DECOMPOSED, BECAUSE A SINGLE NUMBER MISLEADS HERE:
- CONSUMER GENERATIVE-AI PENETRATION: ~1.5-2 YEARS. Indonesia sits at ~14.9% population penetration in 2026; China passed 17.6% at end-2024. This is the narrowest lag in the whole China-Indonesia comparison set and is far tighter than e-commerce (2-3 yrs), fintech (4-6 yrs) or robotics (10+ yrs), because the technology is delivered as free software over an internet base where Indonesia already exceeds China's penetration.
- ENTERPRISE / ORGANIZATIONAL DEPLOYMENT: ~3-4 YEARS. Indonesia ~23-26% organizational implementation versus China's >30% of above-scale manufacturers and ~79% enterprise agent deployment — roughly China's 2023 position.
- STATE DIFFUSION POLICY (the actual subject of this item): 5-10 YEARS, AND POSSIBLY NEVER IN THE SAME FORM. China moved from strategy (2017) to named initiative (2024) to binding numeric targets with sectoral cascade and demand subsidies (2025-2026). Indonesia is still at the 2017-2020 stage of that sequence — a strategy document without enforcement, and a roadmap Perpres that has missed three announced signing deadlines. Even if the Perpres is signed in late 2026, Indonesia would only then be at the 'named initiative' stage China reached in March 2024, and it would still lack the two instruments that actually move penetration: quantified targets assigned to accountable units, and demand-side subsidies.
- HARM-SPECIFIC REGULATION (labelling, minors, deepfakes): ~2-3 YEARS. China's content labelling took effect Sept 2025 and companion-AI rules July 2026; Indonesia has labelling identified as the first implementing rule but nothing in force.
- COMPUTE AND SOVEREIGN CAPABILITY: 8-12 YEARS on any capacity-adjusted measure, and structurally uncloseable at national scale.
BEST SINGLE ANSWER FOR THIS ITEM: 5-7 YEARS on national AI diffusion policy, versus about 2 years on actual consumer usage. The defining feature of this trend is that the POLICY lag is roughly three times the USAGE lag — Indonesian society is adopting AI far faster than the Indonesian state is organising it.
bukti_historical_lag:
(1) THE 'INTERNET+' PRECEDENT IS THE CLEANEST ANALOGUE. China wrote 'Internet+' into the Government Work Report in March 2015 with a cascade of ministerial implementation plans; Indonesia's comparable framing — Making Indonesia 4.0 (2018) and the Peta Jalan Indonesia Digital 2021-2024 — arrived 3-6 years later and, critically, without numeric adoption targets or demand subsidies. The same structural difference is repeating with AI+, which suggests the gap is institutional rather than temporal.
(2) AI STRATEGY ITSELF. China's New Generation AI Development Plan: July 2017. Indonesia's Stranas KA: August 2020 — a 3-year lag on the strategy document, but Stranas KA has produced no binding regulation in six years, so the effective lag on IMPLEMENTED policy is much larger than three years.
(3) DATA-PROTECTION LAW AS A CALIBRATION POINT. China's PIPL took effect November 2021; Indonesia's UU PDP was passed in 2022 with a two-year transition to October 2024 and an implementing regulation and supervisory authority still incomplete well into 2026. Indonesia can pass headline laws close to China's timing but consistently lags by years on implementing regulations, institutions and enforcement — exactly the failure mode now visible with the AI Perpres.
(4) CONSUMER TECHNOLOGY LAGS HAVE BEEN COMPRESSING. Livestream/social commerce: China 2019-2021, Indonesia 2021-2023 (2-3 yrs). QR payments: China 2015-2017, Indonesia (QRIS) 2019-2023 (4-6 yrs). Ride-hailing/gig platforms: ~2 yrs. Generative AI consumer adoption at ~2 yrs is the shortest yet, consistent with the rule that software delivered over the internet transfers fastest and capital-intensive or institution-intensive things transfer slowest.
(5) THE ASYMMETRY THAT DEFINES THIS ITEM. Every prior trend showed Indonesia's lag closing on the USAGE side while remaining wide on the POLICY side (gig-worker protection, platform regulation, fintech supervision all arrived years after the phenomenon). AI+ is the same pattern in a more consequential form: adoption is arriving before the state has any instrument to direct, subsidise, measure or restrain it.
tipe_lag: LAGGARD on state-driven diffusion policy (5-7 years, and structurally so — Indonesia lacks the target-cascade machinery, not merely the timing), NEAR-SIMULTANEOUS on consumer AI usage (~2 years and compressing), and with a genuine LEAPFROG OPTION on capability: because China open-weights its frontier models (DeepSeek, Qwen), Indonesia can obtain in 2026 the model capability China spent tens of billions building, at effectively zero licence cost. The realistic risk is a THIRD pattern — 'adoption without absorption': Indonesian society consumes foreign AI at near-Chinese rates while the Indonesian state neither directs the diffusion, captures the value, nor regulates the harms.
probabilitas_transfer: MASS AI DIFFUSION ITSELF: TINGGI (HIGH) — already happening, market-led. THE CHINESE POLICY MODEL (numeric penetration targets + sectoral action plans + demand-side compute/model vouchers + SOE mandates): RENDAH-SEDANG (LOW-MEDIUM). Selective policy borrowing (AI content labelling, risk tiering, government-adoption roadmaps, sovereign AI fund, WAICO alignment): SEDANG-TINGGI (MEDIUM-HIGH).
alasan_probabilitas:
WHY THE TECHNOLOGY TRANSFERS EASILY (high probability): (a) Delivery is software over the internet at zero marginal cost, into a country with 81.72% internet penetration — higher than China's. (b) The leading Chinese models are OPEN WEIGHT: DeepSeek and Qwen can be downloaded and deployed by any Indonesian firm without permission, price negotiation or export licence; Qwen has the largest open-weight derivative ecosystem on Hugging Face. (c) Chinese vendors are actively selling into Indonesia — Alibaba Cloud, Huawei, Tencent (J&T Express, Traveloka, GDP Venture), with Indosat/AIonOS building DeepSeek-based products. (d) Consumer demand is self-propelling: Indonesia is already a top-15 ChatGPT market and Gen Z adoption is rising fast without any policy push.

WHY THE CHINESE POLICY MODEL LARGELY DOES NOT TRANSFER (low-medium probability): (i) NO TARGET-CASCADE MACHINERY. China's 70%/90% works because targets can be assigned to ministries, provinces, SASAC and SOEs as evaluated performance indicators. Indonesia's state has no comparable instrument for the private sector; the closest analogues (TKDN local-content rules, BUMN directives) apply to procurement and ownership, not technology adoption rates, and Indonesia's post-decentralisation centre-region relationship cannot compel 38 provinces and 500+ regencies onto a common adoption schedule. (ii) NO FISCAL ROOM FOR DEMAND SUBSIDIES. Shanghai alone committed roughly 1.4 billion CNY in municipal AI subsidies; Indonesia's fiscal space in 2026 is dominated by the ~US$15bn free-meals programme, and the proposed Sovereign AI Fund is deferred to 2027-2029 with no committed amount. (iii) NO STATE-OWNED ADOPTION VANGUARD OF EQUIVALENT WEIGHT. China's central SOEs are directed early adopters across heavy industry; Indonesia's BUMN are fewer, more fiscally constrained, and being restructured under Danantara rather than tasked with technology diffusion. (iv) IMPLEMENTATION CAPACITY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT INTENT. The AI Perpres has missed three announced deadlines; Stranas KA produced nothing binding in six years; UU PDP's supervisory authority remains incomplete. A document that cannot be signed cannot cascade. (v) NO COMPUTE OR TALENT BASE TO ABSORB A MANDATE. 580 MW of data-centre capacity and a 400,000-500,000/year talent shortfall mean a 70%-style target would be unmeetable and therefore not credibly set.

WHY SELECTIVE BORROWING IS LIKELY (medium-high): Indonesia has already joined WAICO as a founding member (17 July 2026), imports governance concepts readily (risk tiering echoes both the EU AI Act and Chinese practice; AI content labelling as the first implementing rule directly parallels China's Sept 2025 measures), and has an explicit government-adoption roadmap for 2026-2029 plus a sovereign fund concept that mirrors Chinese state-capital practice. The likely outcome is Chinese-STYLE governance instruments without Chinese-SCALE diffusion instruments.
vektor_transmisi:
(a) OPEN-WEIGHT MODEL DIFFUSION — the dominant and most under-appreciated vector. DeepSeek and Qwen are released under permissive licences; Indonesian firms, universities and government agencies can download and self-host frontier-adjacent capability with no commercial relationship, no data-residency problem, and no procurement process. Indosat/AIonOS is already building DeepSeek-based solutions for tourism, knowledge economy and agriculture. This vector requires no Chinese company to enter Indonesia at all, which makes it both the fastest and the least politically visible route.

(b) DIRECT ENTRY BY CHINESE PLATFORM AND CLOUD VENDORS — Alibaba Cloud (Qwen, Wan video models, multi-city AI talent roadshows, Telkom AI Centre of Excellence partnership), Huawei (partner ecosystem, Ascend compute, Pangu industrial models), Tencent (enterprise AI already deployed at J&T Express, Traveloka, GDP Venture), ByteDance (Tokopedia, plus Doubao's product playbook), Deep Robotics, Unitree and FiberHome. These firms bring not just products but the CHINESE DEPLOYMENT PLAYBOOK — free consumer tier, aggressive vertical agents, subsidised onboarding.

(c) STATE-TO-STATE POLICY DIFFUSION — the newest and most important vector for this specific item. Indonesia's founding membership of the World AI Cooperation Organization (Shanghai, 17 July 2026), signed by the Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, places Indonesia inside a China-anchored AI governance bloc. Expect the transmission of standards, model-evaluation frameworks, governance templates, capacity-building programmes, and the conceptual vocabulary of 'AI+' sectoral action plans through this channel, plus bilateral vehicles such as the Joint Laboratory for Digital Medicine and Proactive Health.

(d) EDUCATIONAL AND TALENT CHANNELS — a proposed Tsinghua University AI branch campus in Indonesia; Alibaba Cloud and Huawei certification pipelines; Indonesian graduates of Chinese universities returning with Chinese-style deployment practice; the Komdigi AI Talent Factory and the Indosat/Nvidia/Cisco AI Centre of Excellence as competing Western-aligned pipelines.

(e) LOCAL COPYCAT AND ADAPTATION — Sahabat-AI is functionally an Indonesian answer to the Chinese sovereign-model logic (national LLM, local languages, open source, state endorsement, telco-backed); Indonesian SaaS vendors are packaging foreign models into WhatsApp-native vertical agents at UMKM price points.

(f) INFRASTRUCTURE AND CAPITAL — Chinese and Chinese-linked data-centre, cloud and GPU investment lowers local inference cost and quietly determines which model families become default.

(g) ALGORITHMIC CONTENT DIFFUSION — TikTok/Douyin-origin AI-usage norms, AI video and companion-app formats, and 'AI+' framing spreading through Indonesian social media well ahead of any policy.

prasyarat_struktural:
CONDITIONS REQUIRED FOR A CHINA-STYLE NATIONAL AI DIFFUSION PROGRAMME, AND INDONESIA'S POSITION ON EACH:

1) CONNECTIVITY BASE — threshold ~75-80% internet penetration. China at AI+ launch (2025): ~80%, 1.125 billion netizens. Indonesia (2026): 81.72%, 235.3 million users. STATUS: MET AND EXCEEDED. Connectivity is emphatically not the constraint.

2) A FREE, LOCALLY-TUNED, MASS-MARKET ASSISTANT. China's consumer surge rests on free apps with excellent Mandarin performance (Doubao 382m MAU, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m by May 2026). Indonesia has Sahabat-AI (open source, Indonesian + regional languages, app released Feb 2026) but nothing at Doubao's distribution scale; most Indonesian usage is ChatGPT in a second language. STATUS: PARTIALLY MET — this is the single biggest lever on the consumer penetration gap (14.9% vs 42.8%).

3) INCOME AND WILLINGNESS TO PAY / SUBSIDISE. China's GDP per capita ~US$13,900 versus Indonesia's ~US$5,400 (about 39%). At consumer level this matters less than expected because the leading Chinese apps are free; at ENTERPRISE level it is decisive, because integration, tuning and governance costs are dollar-denominated while Indonesian wages are not. STATUS: NOT MET at enterprise scale.

4) COMPUTE CAPACITY. China: 1.59 million PFLOPS of intelligent compute (end-2025), >35% of total computing capacity intelligent in 2026, and 1.4 trillion tokens/day of actual consumption. Indonesia: ~580 MW of data-centre capacity, +1.3 GW sought, one sovereign AI data centre and one GB200-class AI factory. STATUS: NOT MET — and grid reliability and power cost outside Java-Bali cap what can be built.

5) STATE CAPACITY TO SET AND CASCADE TARGETS. Requires (a) an accountable subnational hierarchy, (b) evaluated performance indicators, (c) an adoption-mandated state enterprise sector, (d) a measurement apparatus. China has all four. Indonesia has none in usable form: decentralised regional government, no adoption KPIs, BUMN under restructuring, and no national AI-usage statistic beyond an annual APJII survey question. STATUS: NOT MET — and this is a structural feature of Indonesia's political system, not a fixable gap.

6) FISCAL INSTRUMENT FOR DEMAND SUBSIDY. China: provincial compute and model vouchers, 1 trillion RMB state VC fund, Shanghai's ~1.4 billion CNY. Indonesia: Sovereign AI Fund proposed for 2027-2029, unfunded, with fiscal space consumed by the free-meals programme. STATUS: NOT MET.

7) A SIGNED, ENFORCEABLE LEGAL BASIS. Minimum viable: a Presidential Regulation with sanctions, an implementing-agency assignment, and derivative ministerial rules. Indonesia has drafts pending since 2025 with three missed deadlines and reporting that the framework will be guidance-oriented rather than sanction-backed. STATUS: NOT MET — this is the immediate blocker.

8) TALENT TO OPERATE. China: >6,600 AI companies, a deep engineering base. Indonesia: 9 million digital talents needed by 2030 against 100,000-200,000 produced per year. STATUS: SEVERELY UNMET.

9) DATA AND LANGUAGE INFRASTRUCTURE. Public corpora for Bahasa Indonesia and 700+ regional languages, plus digitised sectoral data (health, tax, legal, agriculture) that agents can actually act on. STATUS: EARLY — Sahabat-AI is the main effort; most government data remains un-digitised or siloed, which caps the value of any adoption target.

10) MEASUREMENT. You cannot manage a penetration target you cannot measure. China publishes generative-AI user counts (CNNIC), app MAU (QuestMobile) and daily national token consumption (National Data Bureau). Indonesia's only recurring national AI-usage figure is a single APJII survey question. STATUS: NOT MET — and it is the cheapest of all these gaps to close.

faktor_pembatal_transfer:
STRUCTURAL REASONS THE CHINESE MODEL WILL NOT ARRIVE IN INDONESIA IN THE SAME FORM — regardless of political will:

1) THE TARGET-CASCADE IS A PROPERTY OF THE CHINESE STATE, NOT OF AI POLICY. '70% by 2027' is enforceable because the Party can make it a cadre evaluation criterion for provinces, a KPI for SASAC-supervised SOEs, and a condition of ministerial performance. Indonesia's post-1998 decentralised, coalition-governed, electorally accountable system has no equivalent transmission belt. An Indonesian president can sign a target; he cannot make 38 provinces and hundreds of thousands of firms hit it. This is not a capacity gap that closes with time — it is a different constitution.

2) NO STATE-OWNED INDUSTRIAL VANGUARD OF COMPARABLE WEIGHT. China's diffusion runs first through central SOEs in energy, telecoms, heavy industry and transport that can be ordered to deploy. Indonesian BUMN are fewer, financially strained, and currently being consolidated under Danantara for value recovery rather than tasked as technology adopters.

3) THE ECONOMY BEING DIFFUSED INTO IS DIFFERENT. China is applying AI to the world's largest manufacturing base (over 30% of above-scale manufacturers already adopting) and a vast formal service sector. Indonesia's economy is ~57-58% informal, commodity- and consumption-heavy, with a thin advanced-manufacturing layer. 'AI+ Manufacturing' with 1,000 industrial agents and 100 manufacturing datasets has no Indonesian counterpart to plug into. The high-value diffusion targets simply do not exist in the same density.

4) NO DOMESTIC MODEL INDUSTRY TO CAPTURE THE VALUE. China's 1.2-trillion-yuan core AI industry and 6,600 AI companies mean state-driven demand recycles into domestic capability and jobs. Indonesian adoption sends value to US and Chinese vendors. A Chinese-style diffusion push in Indonesia would function as an import-stimulus programme — which is precisely why the political case for one is weak.

5) COMPUTE SOVEREIGNTY IS UNREACHABLE AT NATIONAL SCALE. 1.59 million PFLOPS versus ~580 MW of general data-centre capacity is not a gap Indonesia closes; it is a gap Indonesia routes around by consuming foreign inference. Any 90%-penetration target would depend on foreign compute, which contradicts the sovereignty framing the policy is sold on.

6) ARCHIPELAGIC GEOGRAPHY AND ELECTRICITY. Uniform national penetration targets are physically implausible where grid reliability, latency and digital literacy vary enormously between Jabodetabek and eastern Indonesia. China's targets assume an integrated national grid and network.

7) MEASUREMENT INFRASTRUCTURE DOES NOT EXIST. China governs diffusion partly because CNNIC, QuestMobile and the National Data Bureau make it visible (602 million users, 499 million app MAU, 1.4 trillion tokens/day). Indonesia has one annual survey question. An unmeasurable target is an unmanageable one, and Indonesian policymakers know it — which is one reason no target has been set.

8) THE HARM-REGULATION HALF ALSO REQUIRES CAPACITY INDONESIA LACKS. China's companion-AI rules worked because CAC could compel ByteDance and Alibaba to shut features within weeks. Indonesian regulators cannot compel OpenAI, Google or ByteDance at that speed, and blunt instruments (platform blocking) carry costs China does not face.
