dampak_lapangan_kerja:
THIS ITEM'S EMPLOYMENT EFFECT IS SECOND-ORDER BUT LARGE, BECAUSE POLICY DETERMINES THE SPEED AND SHAPE OF THE DISPLACEMENT THAT DIFFUSION CAUSES.

JOBS CREATED DIRECTLY BY A DIFFUSION POLICY (the Chinese pattern, if Indonesia follows): AI governance, audit, compliance and risk officers (created by regulation, not by technology); public-sector AI programme managers and data stewards across ministries and regional governments; AI procurement and vendor-management specialists; standards and conformity-assessment professionals (China targets >50 national/industry AI standards by 2026 — each one implies an assessment industry); data-centre engineering, power and cooling technicians tied to the 1.3 GW pipeline; AI trainers, annotators, evaluators and red-teamers, including a genuine Indonesian niche in Bahasa Indonesia and regional-language corpora; AI integration and agent-orchestration engineers in the systems-integrator sector; digital-literacy trainers at scale (the AI Centre of Excellence targets 1 million Indonesians trained by 2027).

JOBS TRANSFORMED IN THE PUBLIC SECTOR — the most Indonesia-specific effect. The 2026-2029 government AI-adoption schedule plus the October 2026 GovTech launch will change what roughly 4.3 million ASN (civil servants) do: routine document processing, data entry, first-line public-service response, verification, and reporting are the first candidates. Indonesian civil-service employment is politically protected, so the realistic outcome is task substitution and hiring freezes at the entry level rather than dismissal — the same 'quiet' pattern China shows in the private sector, transplanted into the bureaucracy.

JOBS DISPLACED BY THE DIFFUSION THE POLICY ENABLES: first-line customer service, back-office administration, data entry, document verification, junior content production, translation, junior design, basic bookkeeping, junior QA. (Detailed treatment belongs to the AI & Labor Automation item; the point here is that a diffusion MANDATE would compress this timeline by years, while the absence of one lets it arrive at market pace.)

THE POLICY-SPECIFIC ASYMMETRY: China's diffusion push at least recycles demand into a 1.2-trillion-yuan domestic AI industry with 6,600 firms and 74% growth in AI job postings, so displaced labour is partly offset by created labour inside the country. If Indonesia mandates adoption without domestic capability, it imports the displacement and exports the job creation — the central employment risk of copying half of the Chinese model. This is the strongest argument for tying any Indonesian adoption incentive to local capability-building (domestic models, local integrators, local data services).
dampak_kelas_menengah:
1) SERVICE QUALITY AND STATE CAPABILITY — the most direct middle-class effect. A functioning GovTech plus AI-enabled public administration would materially improve the things the Indonesian middle class complains about most: permit and licensing times, tax administration, health and education service delivery, and leakage in social programmes. China's diffusion into governance is one of its most visible citizen-facing wins. This is the clearest positive case for Indonesian policy transfer.
2) A NEW PROFESSIONAL CLASS, NARROWLY DISTRIBUTED. AI governance, integration, data and compute roles are high-paying, urban, English-requiring and credential-heavy. They will benefit the upper-middle class that already has access, not the broad middle.
3) POLARISATION BY AI LITERACY. With 81.8% of Indonesian internet users never having used AI, and Gen Z far ahead of other cohorts, diffusion currently rewards the young, urban and English-capable. Without a deliberate literacy programme, mass diffusion widens intra-middle-class inequality rather than narrowing it — the opposite of the QRIS/fintech precedent where a national interoperable standard delivered broad-based benefit.
4) COST OF LIVING AND CONSUMER SURPLUS. Free frontier-adjacent models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Sahabat-AI) hand real capability to Indonesian households and micro-entrepreneurs at zero cost — genuinely progressive, and the single largest middle-class benefit available. Chinese open-weighting is what makes this possible; a closed-model world would have priced Indonesians out.
5) FISCAL EXPOSURE. A Sovereign AI Fund and large compute commitments are middle-class tax money spent on assets with uncertain returns. If AI diffusion is imported rather than built, the middle class pays for infrastructure whose economic rents accrue to foreign vendors.
6) EMPLOYMENT RISK TO THE ENTRY RUNG. The middle class forms through entry-level formal white-collar work, which is exactly what accelerated diffusion compresses. A state-mandated adoption push without labour safeguards would attack the class-formation mechanism directly.
dampak_daerah_non_jawa:
STRUCTURALLY EXCLUSIONARY UNLESS DESIGNED OTHERWISE — and this is where a Chinese-style national target would do the most damage if copied naively.
1) THE PENETRATION GAP IS ALREADY GEOGRAPHIC. APJII's 2026 data show Java continuing to dominate internet penetration and usage; AI usage concentrates further because it correlates with English, tertiary education, formal employment and device quality. A national average penetration target would be met by Java and mask eastern Indonesia entirely — precisely the failure mode of averaged national targets in an archipelagic state.
2) COMPUTE AND CAPABILITY CLUSTER IN THREE PLACES. Data centres, AI factories and talent programmes concentrate in Jabodetabek, Batam and Bali. The 580 MW base and 1.3 GW pipeline are not distributed development; they are enclave infrastructure with high capital and low local employment.
3) LANGUAGE IS THE DECISIVE VARIABLE. Models perform worst in Javanese, Sundanese, Minang, Bugis, Batak and eastern Indonesian languages — so AI is least useful exactly where development need is highest. Sahabat-AI's regional-language coverage is therefore not a nice-to-have; it is the main equity instrument available, and it is the one thing in Indonesian AI policy with no Chinese equivalent problem (China has dialects but a single written standard).
4) THE GENUINE REGIONAL UPSIDE. The most promising AI applications for non-Java are agriculture (crop-yield forecasting is already one of the eight quick-win projects), fisheries, disaster early warning, remote health, and distance education — all of which are stronger use cases outside Java than in it. A diffusion policy organised around SECTORS rather than average penetration would naturally favour the regions.
5) A DELIBERATE SITING LEVER. Data annotation, corpus construction and AI evaluation work is geographically footloose and could be sited in Makassar, Padang, Manado, Malang or Kupang. Alibaba Cloud's precedent of running AI training roadshows into Aceh, Padang, Makassar and Papua shows this is feasible when required as a condition.
6) POWER REMAINS THE HARD LIMIT. Grid reliability and cost outside Java-Bali cap serious compute decentralisation this decade regardless of policy intent.
jurusan_terancam:
This item threatens programs less through automation than through IRRELEVANCE TO THE NEW POLICY AND DEPLOYMENT ECONOMY:
1) PURE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION / ADMINISTRASI NEGARA taught as procedure, filing and manual bureaucratic process — the 2026-2029 government AI-adoption schedule and the GovTech rollout obsolete precisely the routine administrative competencies these programs certify. The field survives only if rebuilt around digital government, service design, data governance and algorithmic accountability.
2) ILMU PERPUSTAKAAN, KEARSIPAN, AND MANAJEMEN PERKANTORAN at the manual-processing level.
3) STATISTIK AND MATEMATIKA taught without computation, and INFORMATIKA taught as syntax-level programming without systems, data, ML or deployment content — the diffusion economy needs integrators and evaluators, not coders of the kind AI already replaces.
4) HUKUM taught as document drafting and rote statute recall, without technology law, data protection, or algorithmic accountability — while AI/data governance law becomes one of the fastest-growing legal specialisms globally.
5) ILMU KOMUNIKASI / JURNALISTIK taught as content production rather than verification, provenance and information integrity — AI content labelling regimes (China's since Sept 2025, Indonesia's planned as the first implementing rule) make verification a regulated professional function.
6) SASTRA / BAHASA ASING AND PENERJEMAHAN in their current form — the clearest casualty internationally, and the field China has cut most aggressively.
7) MANAJEMEN and generic BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION without data, AI-tool fluency or process-redesign content — Indonesia's largest enrolment block producing its most generic graduates.
IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: none of these fields should be closed. The threat is to the LEVEL and the CURRICULUM, not the domain. The Chinese lesson is redesign — keep the discipline, move the human to direction, verification and accountability.
jurusan_dibutuhkan:
POLICY AND GOVERNANCE — the growth area this item creates directly, and the one Indonesia is least prepared for: AI governance, audit and assurance; technology and data-protection law (UU PDP, the incoming Perpres and its derivatives, AI content-labelling compliance); AI ethics and public policy; algorithmic accountability and model-risk management for banks and insurers; AI standards and conformity assessment (China alone is producing >50 national/industry standards by 2026 — every one implies assessors); AI procurement and vendor management for government.

DIGITAL GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC-SECTOR DELIVERY: digital government / GovTech program management; public-sector data governance and interoperability; service design; monitoring-and-evaluation with AI (directly relevant to the eight quick-win projects, from MBG meal monitoring to Koperasi Merah Putih financial tracking).

DEPLOYMENT ENGINEERING, NOT MODEL RESEARCH — the highest-leverage technical category for an AI-importing country: data engineering and pipeline construction (the true binding constraint in Indonesian organisations); MLOps and model operations; AI agent orchestration and systems integration; AI evaluation, benchmarking and quality assurance; retrieval and knowledge-system engineering for Indonesian legal, tax, health and agricultural domains; cybersecurity for AI systems.

LANGUAGE AND DATA SOVEREIGNTY — Indonesia's unique defensible niche: computational linguistics for Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages; corpus construction and curation; low-resource-language NLP; AI evaluation for Indonesian cultural and religious context (including syariah-relevant evaluation). This is where Sahabat-AI must be staffed from and where no foreign lab has an advantage.

PHYSICAL LAYER: data-centre engineering, power systems, thermal/cooling engineering, electrical contracting — the 1.3 GW pipeline is a real, non-offshorable jobs pipeline.

DOMAIN-PLUS-AI HYBRIDS, mirroring China's 2026 catalogue logic ('AI for business', 'data intelligence'): AI in agriculture and food security, AI in health systems, AI in mining and energy, AI in maritime and logistics, AI in education, AI in public finance and tax administration.
china_education_response:
China's education response to AI diffusion is itself a diffusion instrument, and it is far more systematic than anything Indonesia has attempted.
1) 'AI+ EDUCATION' AS A NAMED NATIONAL ACTION PLAN. The Ministry of Education announced the AI+ Education action plan on 10 April 2026, building a comprehensive AI education system spanning primary school through university, with full implementation targeted by 2030. This makes education one of the six AI+ domains rather than a downstream adaptation.
2) COMPULSORY AI EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS. AI instruction has been mandated in primary and secondary education, with Beijing requiring a minimum of eight hours of AI education per academic year for all primary and secondary students from the 2025 autumn semester, and national guidelines pushing AI literacy across the K-12 system. Contrast with Indonesia, where Coding and AI is an OPTIONAL subject under Permendikdasmen 13/2025 and explicitly not required of schools lacking facilities.
3) MASSIVE HIGHER-EDUCATION RESTRUCTURING. Between 2021 and 2025 Chinese universities ended or suspended roughly 12,200 undergraduate programs and introduced roughly 10,200 new ones, executed through the MOE's annual undergraduate major catalogue rather than left to market attrition. AI undergraduate programs went from 35 approved institutions in 2018 to more than 600 universities by 2026. The 2026 catalogue added 38 new majors including AI for business, embodied intelligence, brain-computer science, data intelligence, and low-altitude economy management, with nine universities authorised for embodied intelligence and a new 'interdisciplinary studies' category created for fields that no longer fit the old taxonomy.
4) CURRICULAR REDESIGN OVER CLOSURE. Communication University of China cut five production-oriented programs while creating 'Intelligent Imaging Art'; a 60-year-old Swahili translation course was redesigned so students learn to DIRECT AND MANAGE AI translators. The doctrine is: keep the domain, move the human up to direction, verification and accountability.
5) THE MECHANISM IS THE LESSON. This happened at speed because the MOE controls the national major catalogue and enrolment quotas, permitting annual realignment of higher education to industrial policy. Indonesia's Kemendiktisaintek has a weaker version of the same instrument through prodi accreditation and quota approval, and does not currently use it strategically.
6) WHAT CHINA IS PLAUSIBLY GETTING WRONG: the scale and speed of humanities and foreign-language elimination, and the risk that 600+ AI programs produce a glut of mediocre AI graduates. Indonesia should copy the MECHANISM and the DIRECT-THE-AI curricular philosophy without the scale of humanities destruction.
respons_kebijakan_china:
THE CRITICAL OBSERVATION FOR THIS ITEM: China did NOT wait for diffusion to mature before regulating harms. It runs adoption promotion and harm regulation on parallel tracks, with different agencies owning each. That sequencing is the single most transferable insight.

WHAT CHINA HAS ENACTED, IN ORDER:
1) Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (2023) — licensing/filing, content obligations, security assessment. Established that a provider must be identifiable and accountable BEFORE mass deployment.
2) AI-generated content labelling measures, effective 1 September 2025 — mandatory explicit and implicit labelling of synthetic content, with platform-level duties. Issued at the same moment as the AI+ Opinions: promote adoption and require provenance simultaneously.
3) The AI+ Opinions themselves (26-27 Aug 2025) embed safeguards inside the diffusion mandate — instructing officials to strengthen employment-risk assessment for AI applications and to steer innovation resources toward job-creating directions, with an 'AI + Employment' framework (tax incentives, reskilling, wage subsidies) under discussion.
4) Judicial doctrine on AI-driven dismissal (2025, published as a model case) — adopting AI is not by itself lawful grounds for termination.
5) Interim Measures for the Administration of AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services — issued 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR, effective 15 July 2026. Bans virtual companion and virtual family-member services for minors; requires guardian consent for under-14 users; mandates anti-addiction measures, usage and spending limits, content standards, safety assessments, and heightened protection for elderly users. Crucially it EXEMPTS customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education and research — regulating emotional dependence without touching productivity diffusion. Enforcement was real and fast: Doubao and Qwen shut down personalised companion agents.
6) AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 and a standards programme targeting >50 national/industry AI standards by 2026 — governance delivered through technical standards rather than only through prohibitions.

WHAT INDONESIA SHOULD ADOPT PREEMPTIVELY, IN PRIORITY ORDER: (i) AI-generated content labelling with actual sanctions — already identified as Indonesia's first implementing rule, so the fastest win available; (ii) minors' protection for anthropomorphic/companion AI, BEFORE mass adoption rather than after, since Indonesia's under-18 online population is enormous and the harm arrives with the app not with the policy; (iii) provider accountability and filing for large-scale public-facing AI services; (iv) mandatory employment-impact assessment attached to large-scale public-sector AI deployment; (v) governance through standards and conformity assessment (BSN/SNI) rather than only through a Perpres, because standards scale where enforcement capacity does not; (vi) publish diffusion metrics — a national generative-AI penetration series and public-sector AI deployment register — because China's ability to govern diffusion rests on measuring it.
rekomendasi_kebijakan_indonesia:
1) SIGN THE PERPRES — AND MAKE IT NON-EMPTY. Three tests: a named implementing agency with budget authority, at least one enforceable obligation with a sanction, and a mandatory reporting/measurement mechanism. A guidance-only Perpres after three missed deadlines would confirm Stranas KA's failure mode rather than correct it.
2) DO NOT COPY THE 70%/90% TARGET. Indonesia cannot cascade, subsidise or measure it, and an unmeetable target destroys policy credibility. Set instead SECTOR- AND SERVICE-LEVEL targets that the state actually controls: e.g. all national public services with AI-assisted first-line response by 2029; AI-based leakage monitoring live in MBG and Koperasi Merah Putih by 2027; a fixed number of ministries with published AI deployment registers. Target what you own.
3) SUBSIDISE DEMAND, NOT JUST SUPPLY — the most copyable Chinese instrument. Compute and model vouchers for UMKM and mid-market firms, funded modestly (even a fraction of Shanghai's ~1.4 billion CNY scale would be transformative in Indonesia), delivered through existing MSME channels. This moves adoption faster per rupiah than research grants, and it builds a domestic integrator industry.
4) FUND THE LANGUAGE LAYER AS PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE. Bahasa Indonesia and regional-language corpora, evaluation benchmarks, and domain datasets (health, legal, tax, agriculture) should be state-funded open goods. This is the highest-return, lowest-cost sovereignty investment available and the only one where Indonesia has an absolute advantage. Sahabat-AI should be the vehicle, with sustained funding rather than sponsorship.
5) BUILD MEASUREMENT BEFORE MANDATES. Commission BPS and Komdigi to publish a recurring national generative-AI adoption series (population, enterprise, by province and sector) and require public bodies to register AI deployments. China governs diffusion because CNNIC, QuestMobile and the National Data Bureau make it visible; Indonesia currently has one annual survey question.
6) REGULATE HARMS ON A PARALLEL TRACK, STARTING NOW. Issue the AI content-labelling rule with sanctions; adopt minors' protections for companion/anthropomorphic AI ahead of mass adoption (China's 15 July 2026 measures are a ready template); and require human review plus named accountability for automated decisions in public services, credit and employment. None of this slows adoption — China proves it.
7) TIE INCENTIVES TO LOCAL CAPABILITY. Condition data-centre incentives, government AI procurement and any Sovereign AI Fund disbursement on local hiring, skills transfer, local-language capability and domestic integrator participation. Otherwise a diffusion push is an import-stimulus programme.
8) CAPITALISE THE SOVEREIGN AI FUND EARLIER AND NARROWER. 2027-2029 is late. A smaller fund deployed in 2026-2027 into corpora, public-sector pilots and shared compute for universities and MSMEs would do more than a large fund arriving after the adoption curve has been set by foreign vendors.
9) MAKE CODING AND AI COMPULSORY, WITH TEACHER CAPACITY FIRST. The current optional status guarantees the Java/non-Java gap widens. China mandated it; Indonesia has 97% teacher training participation to build on. Sequence: teacher capacity and devices, then compulsion, with an explicit non-Java rollout schedule.
10) USE WAICO STRATEGICALLY, NOT PASSIVELY. Founding membership is leverage: negotiate for compute access, standards co-development, corpus/tooling transfer and training places, rather than accepting standards adoption as a courtesy. Simultaneously maintain the US-stack hedge — the dual-stack posture (US infrastructure, Chinese open models) is Indonesia's strongest bargaining position and should be made explicit policy.
11) GIVE ONE INSTITUTION CLEAR OWNERSHIP. Fragmentation across Komdigi, Kemenko Perekonomian, BRIN, Danantara and sectoral ministries is repeatedly cited as why the roadmap keeps slipping. Name a single accountable coordinator with convening power over sectoral plans.
peluang_bisnis:
1) AI GOVERNANCE, AUDIT AND COMPLIANCE SERVICES — a market created by regulation, currently near-zero in Indonesia. The Perpres, its three-tier risk classification, mandatory content labelling, risk reporting duties (biometrics, IP, deepfakes) and sectoral derivatives from OJK and Kemenkes will generate demand for assessment, documentation, watermark verification and assurance. First movers with credible methodology will define the market.
2) PUBLIC-SECTOR AI SYSTEM INTEGRATION — the 2026-2029 government adoption schedule, the October 2026 GovTech launch and the eight quick-win projects (MBG monitoring across 83 million beneficiaries, crop-yield forecasting, Koperasi Merah Putih financial tracking) represent a large, budgeted, addressable pipeline for local integrators who understand both government procurement and AI deployment.
3) BAHASA INDONESIA AND REGIONAL-LANGUAGE DATA SERVICES — corpus construction, annotation, evaluation, red-teaming, and domain datasets for Indonesian legal, tax, health, halal and syariah contexts. Labour-intensive, cost-advantaged, sitable outside Java, and the one layer of the stack where foreign labs cannot outcompete Indonesians. Exportable to global labs that need Indonesian coverage.
4) VERTICAL AI AGENTS FOR UMKM AT INDONESIAN PRICE POINTS — the Chinese lesson is that free or near-free consumer-grade tooling drives penetration. Whoever productises WhatsApp-native vertical agents (klinik, distributor, ekspedisi, sekolah, koperasi, warung) at sub-Rp500k/month captures a 65-million-MSME base that no foreign vendor is serving.
5) DEPLOYING CHINESE OPEN-WEIGHT MODELS AS A SERVICE — DeepSeek, Qwen and GLM can be self-hosted for regulated Indonesian clients (banks, government, health) that cannot send data offshore. Sovereign/on-premise inference is a defensible local business precisely because the models are free and the deployment is not.
6) COMPUTE AND DATA-CENTRE ADJACENT SERVICES — with ~580 MW installed and 1.3 GW sought, cooling, power engineering, electrical contracting, colocation operations and specialised staffing are physical, local and non-offshorable.
7) AI LITERACY AND CERTIFICATION AT NATIONAL SCALE — 81.8% of Indonesian internet users have never used AI, and the AI Centre of Excellence targets 1 million trained by 2027 against a 9-million-by-2030 talent requirement. Training tied to employer hiring commitments is a durable business.
8) MEASUREMENT AND MARKET INTELLIGENCE — Indonesia has no QuestMobile or CNNIC equivalent for AI. A credible recurring Indonesian AI adoption index would be bought by vendors, investors and government alike.
9) CONTENT PROVENANCE AND WATERMARKING TOOLING — if labelling becomes the first implementing rule, every platform, broadcaster, agency and publisher in Indonesia needs compliance tooling.
10) EDGE AND LOW-CONNECTIVITY AI FOR NON-JAVA — offline-capable, low-bandwidth AI for agriculture, fisheries, health outposts and schools in regions the mainstream stack ignores.
rekomendasi_individu_mahasiswa:
1) SPECIALISE IN THE GAP BETWEEN POLICY AND DEPLOYMENT. The scarce Indonesian profile is not 'AI engineer' and not 'policy analyst' — it is someone who can read a regulation and build or audit a compliant system. AI governance, audit, evaluation and standards work is a career that barely exists in Indonesia today and will be in structural shortage the moment the Perpres is signed.
2) LEARN DEPLOYMENT, NOT MODEL RESEARCH. Indonesia will import models and build integrations. Data engineering, retrieval systems, agent orchestration, evaluation and MLOps are where the durable, well-paid, non-automatable Indonesian jobs are.
3) WORK ON INDONESIAN-LANGUAGE AI. Contributing to Sahabat-AI, regional-language corpora, Indonesian evaluation benchmarks, or domain datasets builds a credential no foreign competitor can match and sits at the centre of national policy priority.
4) UNDERSTAND GOVERNMENT AS A CLIENT. The 2026-2029 public-sector adoption schedule, GovTech, and the eight quick-win projects make government the largest single AI buyer in Indonesia this decade. Learning public procurement, e-government architecture and programme monitoring is unglamorous and highly employable.
5) READ THE ACTUAL POLICY DOCUMENTS — the State Council AI+ Opinions, China's sectoral action plans, Indonesia's AI White Paper and draft Perpres, and the EU AI Act. Almost nobody in the Indonesian job market has, and comparative policy literacy is a genuine differentiator in consulting, law, government and corporate strategy.
6) BUILD BILINGUAL/TRILINGUAL CAPABILITY INCLUDING MANDARIN. With WAICO membership, Chinese vendors, open-weight Chinese models and a proposed Tsinghua campus, the ability to work directly with Chinese technical and policy material is a rare and rising asset.
7) TREAT FREE CHINESE OPEN MODELS AS YOUR PERSONAL INFRASTRUCTURE. DeepSeek, Qwen and their derivatives give an Indonesian student the same model capability as a Silicon Valley startup at zero cost. The constraint is skill in using and deploying them, not access.
8) GET PROOF OF WORK, NOT JUST CREDENTIALS — shipped projects, open-source contributions to Indonesian-language AI, and public writing. In a market with no established AI-governance profession, visible work IS the credential.
rekomendasi_perguruan_tinggi:
OPEN OR EXPAND: AI Governance, Audit and Technology Law (as a genuine interdisciplinary program, not an elective) — the single largest unmet demand this policy creates; Digital Government / GovTech and public-sector data governance (aligned to the 2026-2029 adoption schedule); Data Engineering and MLOps as a track distinct from Data Science; AI Evaluation and Assurance; Computational Linguistics for Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages; Data Centre and Power Systems Engineering; and applied domain-plus-AI hybrids explicitly modelled on China's 2026 catalogue logic (AI for agriculture and food security, AI in health systems, AI in public finance, AI in maritime and logistics).

REDESIGN RATHER THAN CLOSE: Administrasi Negara around digital government, service design and algorithmic accountability; Hukum around technology, data-protection and AI liability law; Ilmu Komunikasi around verification, provenance and information integrity (a regulated function once content labelling is mandatory); Statistika and Informatika around computation, systems and deployment; Sastra and Penerjemahan around directing and auditing AI language systems — the Chinese Swahili-course model.

INSTITUTIONAL ACTIONS: (1) Make AI literacy a compulsory general-education course for every prodi — the highest-return single intervention, and the direct analogue of China's mandatory K-12 AI education. (2) Establish AI policy and governance research centres capable of independently evaluating the Perpres and its implementing rules; Indonesia currently has almost no domestic capacity to critique its own AI policy. (3) Create a national program-realignment cycle at Kemendiktisaintek modelled on China's MOE catalogue mechanism — evidence-driven, annual, with a deliberate bias toward curricular conversion over closure. (4) Partner with government on the eight quick-win projects as live capstone environments, so students graduate having built real public-sector AI systems. (5) Use WAICO and bilateral channels to secure faculty exchange, joint labs and training places rather than only vendor certification pipelines — and negotiate for capability transfer, not branded courseware. (6) Site AI programs, annotation training and compute access deliberately outside Java, or the national capability map will simply reproduce the existing penetration map.
dampak_negatif_china:
1) TARGET-DRIVEN FORMALISM AND WASTED CAPITAL. Numeric penetration targets assigned to provinces and SOEs create strong incentives to report adoption rather than achieve it — 'AI face projects' (面子工程), demonstration scenarios with no production use, and duplicated local compute centres built for target compliance rather than demand. The pre-existing evidence is stark: only 4.5% of surveyed SOE executives in 2022 said internal digital transformation was meeting expectations and 60% were at an early stage, yet these same firms are the mandated adoption vanguard. Mandating AI adoption onto un-digitised processes automates dysfunction.
2) EMPLOYMENT DISPLACEMENT AS THE POLICY'S OWN CENTRAL RISK. Youth unemployment reached 18.9% in August 2025 and was still 16.9% in March 2026, with employment sentiment at record lows in central bank surveys, and the state's own planners now debating universal basic income and subsidising low-productivity jobs. The diffusion push runs directly against the regime's performance-legitimacy dependence on employment.
3) HARM AT CONSUMER SCALE ARRIVING BEFORE THE GUARDRAILS. Emotional dependence on companion AI reached a scale that required five agencies to intervene, forcing Doubao and Qwen to shut down personalised companion features used by very large numbers of people in July 2026 — with millions losing accumulated chat histories overnight. The regulation was necessary; the fact that it was necessary is the damage report.
4) MINORS AND ELDERLY EXPOSURE. The 2026 companion measures exist because minors were forming relationships with AI systems at scale and elderly users were exposed to manipulation and spending harms.
5) INFORMATION-ENVIRONMENT DEGRADATION. Content labelling became mandatory in September 2025 because synthetic content, deepfakes and AI-generated misinformation had already saturated Chinese platforms.
6) CONCENTRATION AND COMPETITIVE DISTORTION. Free consumer tiers funded by platform balance sheets (Doubao at 382m MAU, >1.2 trillion tokens/day) make sustainable independent competition nearly impossible; diffusion succeeds partly by concentrating the market in a few very large firms.
7) MEASUREMENT DISTORTION. Once penetration becomes a governed target, the statistics measuring it become politically loaded — a general problem with Chinese target-driven policy that makes independent verification of the 2027 '70%' claim effectively impossible.
8) ENERGY AND RESOURCE COST of a compute build-out sized to a 90%-penetration target.
risiko_sosial_indonesia:
1) ADOPTION WITHOUT ABSORPTION — the core risk. Indonesian society is adopting AI faster than the Indonesian state can direct, measure or regulate it. Roughly 42-43 million users already, no signed regulation, no measurement series, no content-labelling rule in force, no minors' protection. Every month of delay locks in foreign default platforms and imported norms.
2) HARMS ARRIVE ON THE VENDOR'S SCHEDULE, NOT THE REGULATOR'S. China needed five agencies and a hard shutdown to address companion-AI dependence among minors. Indonesia has an enormous under-18 online population, weaker parental digital literacy, and no equivalent rule even drafted. Deepfake fraud, AI-generated scams, non-consensual imagery, and election manipulation ahead of 2029 are all live and unaddressed.
3) POLICY THEATRE. The gravest institutional risk is a Perpres that is signed, celebrated, and toothless — repeating Stranas KA (six years, nothing binding) and Surat Edaran 9/2023 (voluntary, unenforced). That outcome would consume the political window while changing nothing.
4) COPYING THE WRONG HALF OF THE CHINESE MODEL. Importing adoption ambition (targets, mandates, sovereign funds) without importing the safeguards (labelling, minors' protection, employment-risk assessment, judicial limits on AI-driven dismissal) would produce the worst available combination: accelerated displacement, foreign value capture, and no protection.
5) DIGITAL DIVIDE HARDENING INTO A CAPABILITY DIVIDE. 81.8% of internet users have never used AI; Java and Gen Z dominate what usage exists. National-average targets would mask and worsen this. AI could become the mechanism that converts Indonesia's connectivity success into a new inequality.
6) FISCAL RISK ON THE SOVEREIGN AI FUND. State capital deployed at scale into AI infrastructure, managed through Danantara, in a country with weak project-selection track records and thin technical evaluation capacity, is an obvious vector for waste and rent-seeking. China's version at least recycles into a domestic industry; Indonesia's may not.
7) DEPENDENCE AND GEOPOLITICAL EXPOSURE. Building the national stack on Chinese open-weight models plus US hyperscaler infrastructure is pragmatic but creates two dependency surfaces simultaneously. Open weights mitigate lock-in but not the dependence on foreign model roadmaps, safety choices, and embedded values — including on topics where Chinese model behaviour reflects Chinese content rules.
8) PUBLIC-SECTOR AI WITHOUT DUE PROCESS. Deploying AI into the MBG programme, cooperative finance tracking and GovTech touches eligibility, benefits and enforcement for tens of millions. Without a right to human review, explanation and appeal, errors become injustices at scale — and Indonesia's draft framework is reported to be guidance-oriented.
9) LANGUAGE AND CULTURAL MARGINALISATION of Indonesia's non-Indonesian-speaking populations if the language layer remains unfunded.
10) TALENT DRAIN. The small pool capable of building this capacity is exactly the pool most employable abroad and by foreign remote employers.
unintended_consequences:
OBSERVED IN CHINA: (1) A diffusion mandate aimed at productivity produced its largest consumer success in EMOTIONAL and entertainment uses — companion AI and AI video — forcing the state to regulate against the very engagement that drove its penetration numbers; the July 2026 companion shutdown removed features from apps the state was otherwise celebrating. (2) Free consumer AI pushed penetration to 42.8% but concentrated the market in a handful of platform giants, making the 'diffusion' partly a platform-consolidation event. (3) Publishing token consumption as a national KPI incentivises token-heavy applications (AI video) over token-light high-value ones — the metric shapes the market. (4) Mandating adoption in poorly digitised SOEs risks automating broken processes and producing measured adoption with no productivity gain. (5) Open-weighting DeepSeek and Qwen to win global mindshare handed Indonesia and the rest of the Global South the capability to reduce dependence on Chinese platforms — a genuine transfer of power that also builds long-run Chinese standard-setting influence. (6) A plan designed to sustain growth against a shrinking workforce is generating the youth-employment problem that most threatens the regime's legitimacy.

PREDICTED FOR INDONESIA: (1) The absence of a diffusion mandate may prove ACCIDENTALLY PROTECTIVE — market-paced adoption gives Indonesian institutions time China did not have, and preserves the option to regulate harms before saturation. Policy failure and policy prudence are indistinguishable here, but the outcome may be favourable. (2) The Perpres, once signed, will most likely be over-implemented as compliance paperwork and under-implemented as capability — Indonesian AI policy could generate a governance industry before it generates an AI industry. (3) Free Chinese open-weight models may do more for Indonesian AI capability than any Indonesian policy, making the most consequential Indonesian AI decision one made in Hangzhou. (4) A national target, if ever set, would be met by Java and reported nationally, hard-coding regional inequality into the official record. (5) Sahabat-AI may succeed technically and fail on distribution, because Indonesia has no equivalent to ByteDance's ability to put an assistant in front of hundreds of millions of users. (6) Public-sector AI (MBG monitoring, cooperative finance tracking) may deliver its first visible win as ANTI-CORRUPTION leakage detection rather than as efficiency — which would make AI politically popular for reasons no roadmap anticipated, and politically dangerous to the interests it exposes. (7) WAICO membership taken as a routine diplomatic signature may quietly determine which technical standards Indonesian regulation converges on for a decade.
kelompok_rentan:
1) THE 81.8% OF INDONESIAN INTERNET USERS WHO HAVE NEVER USED AI — older, less educated, non-English-speaking, and outside Java. As services, government interfaces and commerce become AI-mediated, non-users move from 'not benefiting' to 'excluded'.
2) CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS. Indonesia has a very large under-18 online population, high social-media use, and no companion-AI or minors' protection rule even drafted, while China needed emergency measures effective July 2026 to address exactly this harm. Indonesian minors are currently exposed to a class of harm that a peer state has already judged serious enough to force product shutdowns.
3) NON-JAVA AND RURAL POPULATIONS — worst model performance in their languages, weakest connectivity quality, least compute proximity, and lowest probability of appearing in any national average.
4) SPEAKERS OF REGIONAL LANGUAGES — hundreds of languages with negligible representation in training data; without funded corpora, AI accelerates linguistic marginalisation.
5) CIVIL SERVANTS IN ROUTINE ADMINISTRATIVE ROLES, especially in regional governments, as GovTech and the 2026-2029 adoption schedule automate document processing and first-line service response.
6) BENEFICIARIES OF AI-ADMINISTERED SOCIAL PROGRAMMES — the 83 million people in the free nutritious meals programme and cooperative members subject to AI financial tracking. Automated eligibility, attendance or fraud flags without a guaranteed right to human review and appeal turn technical errors into denied benefits.
7) ELDERLY INDONESIANS — targets of AI-enabled fraud, deepfake scams and manipulative interfaces; China explicitly wrote elderly protection into its 2026 companion measures.
8) INFORMAL AND MICRO-ENTERPRISE WORKERS (57-58% of employment) — outside every adoption programme, outside enterprise tooling, and outside the data on which policy is built.
9) WOMEN IN ADMINISTRATIVE AND CLERICAL ROLES — the occupational category most exposed to the diffusion this policy would accelerate.
10) VICTIMS OF SYNTHETIC MEDIA — with no content-labelling rule in force and a 2029 election cycle approaching, targets of deepfake harassment, fraud and political manipulation have no specific legal remedy.
kasus_china:
CASE 1 — THE STATE COUNCIL 'AI+' OPINIONS, 26-27 AUGUST 2025. The first government document anywhere to attach numeric, dated penetration targets to economy-wide AI adoption: >70% penetration of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents by 2027, >90% by 2030, a 'fully intelligent economy and society' by 2035, across six named domains (science and technology, industry, consumption, public wellbeing, governance, global cooperation). Deliberately modelled on 'Internet+' (2015). Its significance is structural: numeric targets can be cascaded to ministries, provinces and SOEs as performance indicators, converting an aspiration into an administrative programme.

CASE 2 — THE SECTORAL CASCADE OF 2026. The umbrella plan became real through ministry-level implementation: MIIT with eight agencies on 'AI+ Manufacturing' to 2027 (3-5 general-purpose industrial models, 1,000 industrial intelligent agents, 100 high-quality manufacturing datasets, 500 demonstration scenarios); MOFCOM with seven departments on 'AI+ Consumption' (18 June 2026); MOE on 'AI+ Education' (10 April 2026, full implementation by 2030); MIIT targeting >50 national and industry AI standards by 2026. This is the mechanism Indonesia most conspicuously lacks.

CASE 3 — SHANGHAI'S DEMAND-SIDE SUBSIDIES. Roughly 900 million CNY for enterprise access to computing clusters, models and training data, plus around 500 million CNY over three to five years for company innovation — one city paying firms to CONSUME AI. Compute vouchers and model vouchers are the most transferable instrument in the whole Chinese playbook because they attack the buyer-side cost barrier that actually limits diffusion.

CASE 4 — THE CONSUMER FLYWHEEL. CNNIC's 57th report (5 Feb 2026): 602 million generative-AI users, 42.8% of the population, +141.7% year-on-year from 249 million (17.6%) at end-2024. QuestMobile: AI-native apps at 499 million MAU by May 2026 (+85.4% YoY), Doubao 382m, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m, with users averaging 92.7 sessions and 183 minutes per month. In August 2025 the same series showed Doubao at 157 million and DeepSeek at 143 million — meaning Doubao alone added roughly 225 million MAU in nine months. Free pricing plus excellent native-language performance, not policy, is what produced this.

CASE 5 — TOKEN CONSUMPTION AS A GOVERNED METRIC. National Data Bureau Director Liu Liehong, China Development Forum, 23 March 2026: daily national token invocation exceeded 1.4 trillion, up from about 100 billion in early 2024 — more than a thousandfold in two years, with Doubao alone above 1.2 trillion tokens/day by April 2026. The state publishing a real-time diffusion metric is itself the policy innovation: what is measured can be targeted.

CASE 6 — THE COMPANION-AI SHUTDOWN, 15 JULY 2026. Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services (issued 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR) banned virtual companion and virtual family-member services for minors, required guardian consent under 14, and imposed anti-addiction, spending and duration controls — while explicitly exempting customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education and research. Doubao and Qwen shut down personalised companion agents. This is the cleanest demonstration anywhere that a state can regulate a specific AI harm hard and fast WITHOUT slowing productive diffusion.

CASE 7 — THE SOE CONTRADICTION. In 2022, only 4.5% of surveyed SOE executives said internal digital transformation was meeting expectations and 60% described their firms as at an early stage — yet these are the enterprises the state most wants leading AI adoption. The gap between mandate and absorptive capacity is the strongest available evidence that penetration targets do not by themselves produce productivity.
padanan_indonesia:
Indonesia has a partial analogue to each Chinese case, all weaker and all later:
- STATE COUNCIL AI+ OPINIONS → the two draft Perpres (National AI Roadmap and AI Ethics/Governance) plus the 179-page White Paper. UNSIGNED as of August 2026 after at least three missed deadlines, with no numeric penetration target and reportedly guidance-rather-than-sanction oriented. Indonesia's older analogue, Stranas KA 2020-2045, produced no binding regulation in six years.
- SECTORAL CASCADE → does not exist. Ministries are described as continuing separate initiatives while the unified roadmap is repeatedly delayed. The closest thing is the 2026-2029 government-body adoption schedule in the draft Perpres and the eight 'quick win' projects.
- DEMAND-SIDE SUBSIDIES → none. The proposed Sovereign AI Fund under Danantara (>US$900bn AUM) is scheduled for 2027-2029, uncapitalised, and oriented to research, public pilots and infrastructure rather than to firm-level adoption vouchers.
- CONSUMER FLYWHEEL → real but shallower: ~42-43 million users, 18.2% of internet users, ~14.9% of population versus China's 42.8%; Indonesia is a top-15 global ChatGPT market. The missing ingredient is a free, excellent, Indonesian-language mass-market assistant — Sahabat-AI (Indosat/GoTo/Nvidia, app released February 2026) is the attempt, at a fraction of Doubao's distribution.
- TOKEN/DIFFUSION METRIC → nothing. Indonesia's only recurring national AI-usage number is a single APJII survey question. No enterprise adoption series, no public-sector AI register, no compute utilisation figure.
- COMPANION-AI AND CONTENT REGULATION → content labelling is identified as the FIRST implementing rule under the coming Perpres, which would parallel China's September 2025 measures, but nothing is in force and no minors'/companion-AI rule is drafted.
- SOE ADOPTION VANGUARD → GovTech/INA Digital national launch October 2026 with ~80% system connectivity and AI-processed data integration across eight ministries is the nearest equivalent, but it is a government-services programme, not an industrial adoption mandate.
- POLICY-BLOC ALIGNMENT → Indonesia as a FOUNDING MEMBER of WAICO (Shanghai, 17 July 2026) with 28 other economies, signed by Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto — the single strongest institutional link, and the most likely channel for future Chinese-style instruments to arrive.
- EDUCATION CASCADE → Permendikdasmen 13/2025 making Coding and AI an OPTIONAL subject (grades 5, 7, 10 from 2025/2026, not required where facilities are lacking; 97% teacher self-training participation by July 2026) versus China's compulsory K-12 AI education and MOE 'AI+ Education' plan to 2030.

catatan_kontradiksi_data:
1) THE 70%/90% TARGET IS NOT OPERATIONALLY DEFINED. Public sources uniformly report 'penetration of new-generation intelligent terminals and AI agent applications' exceeding 70% (2027) and 90% (2030), but no source specifies the denominator — 70% of what? Enterprises? Key-sector firms? Devices shipped? Users? Secondary reporting freely substitutes 'AI adoption across key sectors', which is a materially different claim. Treat the numbers as real policy signals whose achievement will be unverifiable externally.
2) INDONESIAN AI ADOPTION FIGURES ARE MUTUALLY IRRECONCILABLE. APJII 2026: 18.2% of internet users have used AI. Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026: 33% of Indonesian workers are 'Frontier Professionals' (double the global average). Vendor material: '92% workplace AI adoption — the world's highest' and '62% of Indonesian companies will adopt AI'. These measure different populations (all internet users vs employed workers vs enterprises), different intensities (ever-used vs daily vs implemented), and in the 92% case are almost certainly marketing artefacts. The APJII figure is the only nationally representative one and should be preferred; the 92% figure should not be used at all.
3) CHINA'S OWN ADOPTION FIGURES CONFLICT WITH ITS DIGITISATION BASELINE. Reported enterprise AI-agent deployment of ~79% sits awkwardly with >30% of above-scale manufacturers adopting AI and with the 2022 SOE finding that only 4.5% considered digital transformation to be meeting expectations. 'Deployment' in surveys frequently means any pilot; the production-scale figure (~23%) is far more plausible.
4) DEEPSEEK MAU IS DECLINING WHILE ITS INFLUENCE GROWS. DeepSeek fell from 143m MAU (Aug 2025) to 130m (May 2026) even as its open weights became a global default. Consumer MAU is therefore a poor proxy for a model's diffusion impact — the research brief's framing of DeepSeek as a mass-consumer phenomenon understates its actual role as infrastructure.
5) TOKEN CONSUMPTION IS BOTH THE BEST AND THE MOST GAMEABLE METRIC. 1.4 trillion tokens/day is impressive, but Doubao alone accounts for >1.2 trillion of it and the growth is attributed largely to multimodal VIDEO generation. Token volume therefore measures compute intensity of the dominant consumer app more than it measures economy-wide productive diffusion.
6) CHINA'S OPENROUTER 'LEAD' IS A NARROW SAMPLE. Claims that Chinese models surpassed US models globally rest on OpenRouter share, which captures a small, developer-skewed slice of world inference and excludes first-party OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Azure traffic.
7) INDONESIAN ECONOMIC PROJECTIONS DIVERGE WIDELY: 12% of GDP / US$366bn by 2030 (draft Perpres) versus a 3.67% GDP uplift (separate government-cited estimate) versus a US$10.9bn Indonesian AI market by 2030. These cannot all be right; the 12%/US$366bn figure in particular appears to be an economy-wide impact estimate being cited as if it were a policy target.
8) THE PERPRES TIMELINE HAS SLIPPED REPEATEDLY: announced for early 2026, then H1 2026, then 'soon' after clearing harmonisation; reported at various times as sitting with the Ministry of Law and with the State Secretariat. Any statement about its status carries a short shelf life.
9) THE ROADMAP PERIOD IS REPORTED INCONSISTENTLY as 2026-2029 and 2026-2030 across outlets, which matters because it determines whether the plan aligns with the presidential term (2029) or with the China/global 2030 horizon.
10) CHINA'S POSTURE IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY BY DESIGN. The same state that mandates 90% AI penetration by 2030 forced its two largest AI apps to shut down popular features in July 2026 and had courts rule that AI adoption is not lawful grounds for dismissal. Both are genuine policy; treating either in isolation misrepresents the model.
11) A DEFINITIONAL CAUTION ON THE RESEARCH BRIEF ITSELF: DeepSeek at 143m and Doubao at 157m MAU are correct for August 2025, but by May 2026 the ranking and magnitudes had changed substantially (Doubao 382m, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m). Any analysis anchored on the August 2025 snapshot is nine months stale and understates both the pace of diffusion and Alibaba's rise.
